---- MODULE W4Od14m4p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Stations, Pool, Quota

VARIABLES flying, pending

vars == <<flying, pending>>

RECURSIVE SumOver(_, _)
SumOver(f, S) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE
       IN f[x] + SumOver(f, S \ {x})

TotalFlying == SumOver(flying, Stations)

Init ==
  /\ flying = [s \in Stations |-> 0]
  /\ pending = [s \in Stations |-> Quota]

Launch(s) ==
  /\ TotalFlying < Pool
  /\ pending[s] > 0
  /\ flying' = [flying EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
  /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![s] = @ - 1]

Recover(s) ==
  /\ flying[s] > 0
  /\ flying' = [flying EXCEPT ![s] = @ - 1]
  /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]

Transfer(s, r) ==
  /\ s # r
  /\ pending[s] > 0
  /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![s] = @ - 1, ![r] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED flying

GroundAll(s) ==
  /\ flying[s] > 0
  /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![s] = @ + flying[s]]
  /\ flying' = [flying EXCEPT ![s] = 0]

Next ==
  \/ \E s \in Stations : Launch(s)
  \/ \E s \in Stations : Recover(s)
  \/ \E s, r \in Stations : Transfer(s, r)
  \/ \E s \in Stations : GroundAll(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

PoolCapacityRespected == TotalFlying <= Pool
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS Stations = {s1, s2} Pool = 3 Quota = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT PoolCapacityRespected
nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm is run by two independent ground stations that both draw drones from one single shared hangar pool of fixed size. Each station keeps a private set of pending imaging tasks and a count of drones it currently has airborne; launching a drone moves one task from that station's pending set into the air, and recovering a drone returns it to pending, so every station's task total is conserved. A station may launch a drone only when the combined number of drones airborne across both stations is still strictly below the shared pool size, which is the backpressure that keeps the pool from being oversubscribed. A station may recover any of its own airborne drones at any time. Because the two stations share one pool, either station may also transfer one of its pending tasks to the other station to rebalance load without changing anything airborne. Finally, a station may execute an emergency ground command that immediately lands every drone it has airborne, returning them all to its pending set at once. The stations act asynchronously and coordinate on nothing except the shared pool-size limit.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the combined number of drones airborne across both stations is always at most the shared hangar pool size.

  /\ timesRead = [p \in Patrons |-> 0]
  /\ lastReader = None

Acquire(p) ==

  /\ timesRead[p] < ReadLimit
  /\ holder = None

  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![p] = "holding"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<timesRead, lastReader>>

BeginRead(p) ==

  /\ holder = p
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![p] = "reading"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, timesRead, lastReader>>

EndRead(p) ==
  /\ mode[p] = "reading"
  /\ holder = p
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![p] = "idle"]
  /\ holder' = None
  /\ timesRead' = [timesRead EXCEPT ![p] = @ + 1]
  /\ lastReader' = p

Cancel(p) ==
  /\ mode[p] = "holding"
  /\ holder = p
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![p] = "idle"]
  /\ holder' = None
  /\ UNCHANGED <<timesRead, lastReader>>

Quiesce ==

CONSTANTS Patrons = {p1, p2} None = NONE ReadLimit = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT ReadingImpliesHolder
nl:
A library runs an online reservation desk for a single rare book that only one patron may read at a time. Availability is tracked by one shared register that either names the patron currently holding the book or is empty. A patron reserves the book with an atomic compare-and-swap: the reservation succeeds only if the register is currently empty, in which case it is set to that patron in one indivisible step. Holding the book is not the same as reading it: after a successful reservation the patron is in a holding state and must take a separate step to actually begin reading. While reading, the patron occupies the critical reading room. When finished, the patron ends the session, which clears the shared register and records that patron as the last reader and bumps their personal read count. A holding patron who changes their mind may cancel instead, which also clears the register without a read. Patrons act at their own pace and some may be slow, but none ever fail outright, so the register is only ever cleared by whoever currently holds it. Once every patron has used up their allowed number of reads the desk simply idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: at any moment at most one patron is in the reading state, because a patron can be reading only while the shared register names that same patron.

---- MODULE W4Od4m2p2t3 ----
EXTENDS Integers

CONSTANTS Stations, Total, None

VARIABLES intake, load, exited, cphase, target

vars == <<intake, load, exited, cphase, target>>

RECURSIVE SumOver(_, _)
SumOver(f, S) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE
       IN f[x] + SumOver(f, S \ {x})

InFlight == IF cphase = "prepared" THEN 1 ELSE 0

Init ==
  /\ intake = Total
  /\ load = [s \in Stations |-> 0]
  /\ exited = 0
  /\ cphase = "idle"
  /\ target = None

Prepare(s) ==
  /\ cphase = "idle"
  /\ intake > 0
  /\ intake' = intake - 1
  /\ cphase' = "prepared"
  /\ target' = s
  /\ UNCHANGED <<load, exited>>

Commit ==
  /\ cphase = "prepared"
  /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![target] = @ + 1]
  /\ cphase' = "idle"
  /\ target' = None
  /\ UNCHANGED <<intake, exited>>

Abort ==
  /\ cphase = "prepared"
  /\ intake' = intake + 1
  /\ cphase' = "idle"
  /\ target' = None
  /\ UNCHANGED <<load, exited>>

Exit(s) ==
  /\ load[s] > 0
  /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![s] = @ - 1]
  /\ exited' = exited + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<intake, cphase, target>>

Quiesce ==
  /\ cphase = "idle"
  /\ intake = 0
  /\ \A s \in Stations : load[s] = 0
  /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
  \/ \E s \in Stations : Prepare(s)
  \/ Commit
  \/ Abort
  \/ \E s \in Stations : Exit(s)
  \/ Quiesce

====

CONSTANTS Stations = {a, b} Total = 3 None = NONE
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CarsConserved
nl:
An automated car-wash runs a conveyor that moves cars through a set of wash stations under a two-phase commit protocol. A fixed number of cars exist in the system and are never created or destroyed: each car is either waiting in the intake lane, sitting at some wash station, in flight during a handoff, or already driven off the exit. To move a car from intake onto a station the coordinator runs two phases. In the prepare phase it pulls one car out of the intake lane and holds it in flight while it selects a target station and waits for readiness. In the commit phase it places the in-flight car onto the chosen station, or if the station balks it aborts and returns the in-flight car to the intake lane. A car at any station may finish its wash and exit the conveyor. Stations and the coordinator run asynchronously and may be slow, but nothing ever fails, so a handoff that is prepared is always eventually either committed or aborted. Because every step just relocates one car, the census of cars is preserved at all times.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of cars in the intake lane, at the stations, in flight, and already exited always sums to exactly the fixed total number of cars.

INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT AtMostOneLaunch
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker arranges its nodes in a ring and circulates a single token around that ring; only the node currently holding the token is allowed to take the exclusive action of launching the match. The token is passed hand to hand around the ring one hop at a time and this passing may happen at any moment. Each node has a readiness flag that its player may raise or lower at will, modelling a slow but never-failing participant. Launching the match is irreversible: it can happen at most once for the whole lobby. A node may launch the match only when it holds the token, when every node in the lobby is currently ready, and when no launch has yet occurred, recorded by a shared launcher register that starts empty. The launch atomically sets the launcher register to the launching node and marks that node as having performed the launch. Because the launcher register can only be filled while it is still empty, and it is set to whoever performs the launch, no second node can ever record a launch.
SAFETY PROPERTY: at most one node ever performs the match launch, since any node marked as having launched must equal the single node named in the shared launcher register.

  /\ committed = [b \in Bags |-> None]
  /\ leader = None
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ alive = [c \in Controllers |-> TRUE]

Elect(c) ==

  /\ leader' = c
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<assignment, committed, alive>>

FailLeader ==

  /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![leader] = FALSE]
  /\ leader' = None
  /\ UNCHANGED <<assignment, committed, epoch>>

Recover(c) ==

  /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<assignment, committed, leader, epoch>>

  /\ alive[c]
  /\ assignment[b] = None
  /\ assignment' = [assignment EXCEPT ![b] = ch]
  /\ committed' = [committed EXCEPT ![b] = ch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, alive>>

  \/ FailLeader

INIT Init
NEXT Next

nl:
An airport baggage router is driven by two interchangeable controller instances that share one common pool of bags. At any time at most one controller acts as the elected leader, and leadership can fail over: the current leader can go down, after which a healthy controller is elected as the new leader under a fresh, higher epoch number. Only the live elected leader may route a bag, and routing a bag to a chute is irreversible and must happen at most once per bag. When the leader routes a bag it atomically records the chosen chute both as that bag's current assignment and as its permanently committed chute, and it may only route a bag whose assignment is still empty. A controller that has gone down can later recover and become electable again. Each election bumps the epoch number, and the model explores runs up to a bounded epoch ceiling. Because a bag is routed only while unassigned and its committed chute is fixed at that moment, a bag's assignment can never disagree with the chute it was first committed to.
SAFETY PROPERTY: once a bag has been routed its current chute assignment always equals the single chute it was originally committed to, so no bag is ever routed a second time to a different chute.

  /\ admittedCount[n] < Limit

  /\ pending' = pending \ {n}
  /\ admittedCount' = [admittedCount EXCEPT ![n] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED token

  /\ lobby' = lobby \ {n}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, pending, admittedCount>>

  \/ \E n \in Nodes : SendJoin(n)

CONSTANTS N = 3 Cap = 2 Limit = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CapacityRespected
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker seats players into a single lobby of bounded capacity, with its server nodes arranged in a ring that passes one token hop by hop. Each node corresponds to one player. Players send join requests that accumulate in a pending pool, and because these requests travel over an unreliable network they may be picked up and processed in any order, not the order they were sent. A node may admit its own player into the lobby only while it currently holds the ring token, only if that player has a pending request, and only if the lobby is not already full. Admitting moves the player from the pending pool into the lobby and increments how many times that node has been admitted, which is capped so the system stays finite. A seated player may leave the lobby at any time, freeing a seat. The token keeps circulating regardless of everything else, so there is always a next step. The whole point of gating admission on lobby fullness is that the lobby can never hold more players than its capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of players seated in the lobby is always less than or equal to the lobby capacity.

EXTENDS Integers

CONSTANTS Machines, Agents, TotalCans, TTL0, MaxCap, None

VARIABLES depot, stock, soldBin, lease, ttl, cap

vars == <<depot, stock, soldBin, lease, ttl, cap>>

SumOver(f, S) ==

  ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE
       IN f[x] + SumOver(f, S \ {x})

Init ==
  /\ depot = TotalCans
  /\ stock = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
  /\ soldBin = 0
  /\ lease = None
  /\ ttl = 0
  /\ cap = [m \in Machines |-> MaxCap]

AcquireLease(a) ==
  /\ lease = None
  /\ lease' = a
  /\ ttl' = TTL0
  /\ UNCHANGED <<depot, stock, soldBin, cap>>

Tick ==
  /\ ttl > 0
  /\ ttl' = ttl - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<depot, stock, soldBin, lease, cap>>

ExpireLease ==
  /\ ttl = 0
  /\ lease # None
  /\ lease' = None
  /\ UNCHANGED <<depot, stock, soldBin, ttl, cap>>

Load(a, m) ==
  /\ lease = a
  /\ ttl > 0
  /\ depot > 0
  /\ stock[m] < cap[m]
  /\ depot' = depot - 1
  /\ stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![m] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<soldBin, lease, ttl, cap>>

Buy(m) ==
  /\ stock[m] > 0
  /\ stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![m] = @ - 1]
  /\ soldBin' = soldBin + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<depot, lease, ttl, cap>>

Reconfigure(m, k) ==
  /\ k \in 1..MaxCap
  /\ cap' = [cap EXCEPT ![m] = k]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<depot, stock, soldBin, lease, ttl>>

Next ==
  \/ \E a \in Agents : AcquireLease(a)
  \/ Tick
  \/ ExpireLease
  \/ \E a \in Agents, m \in Machines : Load(a, m)
  \/ \E m \in Machines : Buy(m)
  \/ \E m \in Machines, k \in 1..MaxCap : Reconfigure(m, k)

CONSTANTS Machines = {m1, m2} Agents = {r1, r2} TotalCans = 3 TTL0 = 2 MaxCap = 2 None = NONE
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CansConserved
nl:
A network of vending machines is served by restocking agents that move cans out of a central depot into the machines, from which customers buy them. Every can in the system is conserved: at all times a can is either sitting in the depot, loaded in one of the machines, or already dropped into the sold bin, and cans are never created or destroyed. Restocking is coordinated by a single lease with an expiry timer: an agent may take the lease only while it is free, which starts a countdown, and the agent may load cans only while it holds the lease and the timer has not yet run out. Each tick decrements the timer, and once it reaches zero the lease may be reclaimed and handed to another agent. An agent loads a can by taking it from the depot into a chosen machine, but only if that machine is below its current capacity. Customers buy cans, moving them from a machine into the sold bin. Machine capacities can be reconfigured at runtime to any value in the allowed range, which affects future loading but never changes how many cans exist.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of cans in the depot, loaded across all machines, and in the sold bin always sums to exactly the fixed total number of cans in the network.

EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Trains, Blocks, Controllers, Dispatchers, Quorum, None

VARIABLES owner, pos, propTrain, propBlock, votes

  /\ owner = [b \in Blocks |-> None]
  /\ pos = [t \in Trains |-> None]
  /\ propTrain = None
  /\ propBlock = None
  /\ votes = {}

Propose(d, t, b) ==
  /\ propTrain = None
  /\ owner[b] = None
  /\ pos[t] = None
  /\ propTrain' = t
  /\ propBlock' = b
  /\ votes' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, pos>>

Vote(c) ==
  /\ propTrain # None
  /\ c \notin votes
  /\ votes' = votes \cup {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, pos, propTrain, propBlock>>

CommitGrant ==
  /\ propTrain # None
  /\ Cardinality(votes) >= Quorum
  /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![propBlock] = propTrain]
  /\ pos' = [pos EXCEPT ![propTrain] = propBlock]
  /\ propTrain' = None
  /\ propBlock' = None
  /\ votes' = {}

Release(t) ==
  /\ pos[t] # None
  /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![pos[t]] = None]
  /\ pos' = [pos EXCEPT ![t] = None]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<propTrain, propBlock, votes>>

AbortProposal ==
  /\ propTrain # None
  /\ propTrain' = None
  /\ propBlock' = None
  /\ votes' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, pos>>

Next ==
  \/ \E d \in Dispatchers, t \in Trains, b \in Blocks : Propose(d, t, b)
  \/ \E c \in Controllers : Vote(c)
  \/ CommitGrant
  \/ \E t \in Trains : Release(t)

CONSTANTS Trains = {t1, t2} Blocks = {b1, b2} Controllers = {x1, x2, x3} Dispatchers = {d1, d2} Quorum = 2 None = NONE
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT OwnershipConsistent
nl:
A subway signalling system divides the track into discrete blocks, and two independent dispatcher instances share the one common pool of blocks and trains. A train may occupy a block only after it is granted that block, and a grant is decided by quorum voting among a set of signal controllers. To start a grant, either dispatcher proposes assigning a currently free block to a train that is not already positioned, provided no other proposal is in progress. Controllers then cast votes for the standing proposal, each controller voting at most once. Once the proposal has collected at least a quorum of votes, the grant commits: the block records that train as its owner and the train records that block as its position, and the proposal is cleared. A train that holds a block may release it, clearing both the block's owner and the train's position. A standing proposal may also be aborted, clearing it without granting. Because a block can be proposed only while it has no owner, and committing sets the block's owner and the train's position together, a train's position block always names that same train as its owner.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a train is positioned on a block, that block's recorded owner is that very train, so no block is ever allocated to two trains at once.

nl:
A subway signalling system allocates track blocks to trains and periodically reconfigures itself under a monotonically increasing epoch number. Each block records which train, if any, owns it, and each train records which block, if any, it is positioned on. A healthy train may allocate a block only if that block currently has no owner and the train is not already positioned; allocation records the train as the block's owner, records the block as the train's position, and stamps the train with the current epoch. A positioned healthy train may release its block, clearing both the owner and the position. The controller may reconfigure at any time, which simply advances the epoch number; the model explores runs up to a bounded epoch ceiling. Any train may crash silently and permanently: it simply stops taking part, and after crashing it never allocates or releases again, though whatever block it already held stays owned by it. Because a block is allocated only while it has no owner, and allocation sets the block's owner and the train's position in the same step, a train's position block always records that same train as its owner.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a train is positioned on a block, that block's recorded owner is that very train, so the same block is never allocated to two different trains.

A print shop spools jobs that all contend for one single physical printer, the critical resource that only one job may use at a time. Acquiring the printer runs a two-phase commit across a fixed set of resource managers. To start, an idle job opens a transaction, provided the printer lock is currently free and no other transaction is already in progress. Each resource manager then casts its vote for the open transaction, each voting at most once. The transaction commits only once every resource manager has voted, at which point the printer lock is granted to that job and the job moves into the printing state. Alternatively the open transaction may abort, returning the job to idle and leaving the lock free. A job that is printing may finish, which releases the printer lock and returns the job to idle. The whole protocol exists to guarantee that a job may be in the printing state only while it is the holder of the single printer lock.

A waiting student may be admitted into a course only while the course still has a free seat, that is while its enrollment is strictly below its capacity; admission moves the student from the waitlist into the enrolled set. To count a seated, not-yet-counted player in, that player first claims the shared register with a compare-and-swap that succeeds only while the register is empty. Holding the register, the player commits: its points are added to the shared pool, it is marked counted, and the register is released.   /\ propFrom = None
  /\ propTo = None

  /\ a # b

  /\ propFrom' = a
  /\ propTo' = b
  /\ votes' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED tickets

  /\ v \notin votes
  /\ votes' = votes \cup {v}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tickets, propFrom, propTo>>

  /\ propFrom # None
  /\ Cardinality(votes) >= Quorum
  /\ tickets' = [tickets EXCEPT ![propFrom] = @ - 1, ![propTo] = @ + 1]
  /\ propFrom' = None
  /\ propTo' = None
  /\ votes' = {}

AbortMove ==
  /\ propFrom # None
  /\ propFrom' = None
  /\ propTo' = None
  /\ votes' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED tickets

A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker distributes a fixed pool of entry tickets across its lobbies, and two independent matchmaker instances share that one common pool. Every ticket is conserved: the total number of tickets held across all lobbies never changes, tickets are only ever moved, never created or destroyed. Moving a ticket from one lobby to another is a governed action decided by quorum voting among a set of referees. Either matchmaker instance may open a proposal to move one ticket from a source lobby that has at least one ticket to a different destination lobby, provided no proposal is already open. Referees then vote on the open proposal, each voting at most once. Once the proposal has gathered at least a quorum of votes, the move commits atomically: one ticket leaves the source lobby and one ticket arrives at the destination lobby in the same step, and the proposal is cleared. An open proposal may instead be aborted, clearing it with no movement. Because the only way tickets ever change hands is this atomic one-out-one-in commit, the total ticket count is preserved at all times.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the sum of tickets held across all lobbies always equals the fixed total size of the ticket pool.

Each live interlocking participant then votes on the open transaction, voting at most once. Holding the coarse lock, the job then grabs the fine lock on some free press and begins printing on it, releasing the coarse lock in the same step so other jobs can proceed. A privileged administrator may override the entire spooler at once, force-releasing the coarse lock, every press's fine lock, and stopping every printing job.
